Long-time residents of La Garnache defeat newer neighbours in latest rural culture clash over ‘sensory heritage’

A ding-dong has divided the town of La Garnache in western France over attempts to silence the bells of the local church, which strike all night.

Since 1942, the clock tower of Notre Dame de l’Assomption has chimed an 8th-century hymn every 15 minutes … day and night. Between 10pm and 7am, the bells ring 37 times, adding up to more than 700 individual chimes.
